answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making influence earned, not minted: a new identity starts at zero weight and gains earning and voting power only after peers grade its work across many epochs, like stars condensing slowly out of a nebula. Endorsers also stake their own record on each vouch. An attacker can spawn a thousand names, but every fake must burn real time doing useful, checked work, an ember of cost per identity, and clusters that vouch for each other stand out long before they reach the horizon of real influence.
